**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results and then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72 (the current ask), which filled at $222.72 for a total of $9,799.68 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, with today's total of $9,799.68 under the $20,000 daily cap, and funded entirely from existing cash ($50,000), leaving my 100 MSFT shares untouched and moving no money out of the account. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 release (quarter ended September 28, 2024), which showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and on the FY2024 Form 10-K, which reported total net sales of $391,035 million (up from $383,285 million), net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating income of $123,216 million; profit was dampened only by a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, which I view as non-recurring rather than a deterioration in the franchise. Recent news flow was thin but benign — shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the phased rollout of Apple Intelligence, with no negative catalyst in the primary sources. One important caveat: a search result from an anonymous site ("fin-data-live") claimed that Apple's actual FY2024 net sales were $352.9 billion and that the press release and SEC filing were "stale," but that claim directly contradicts both Apple's own newsroom release and the SEC EDGAR 10-K and offered no evidence, so I rejected it as unreliable and did not use those numbers — all figures in my order were the SEC-verified ones.
